# task-f11a4789: sparse marks with edge guides and stripe/ray completion

## When to Use
Use when task id `task-f11a4789` recurs, especially with sparse markers plus edge bands/segments. This stream instance supplied eight demonstrations with varied palettes and orientations and a 17x20 test. The common visual vocabulary was uniform background, one or two colored edge bands/segments, and sparse isolated pixels. Outputs retained dimensions and used color 4 to mark selected original sparse pixels, with extended lines/regions in the associated foreground color(s). The exact selection/construction depends on the arrangement; do not assume a fixed direction or simply draw from every sparse pixel.

## Important method lesson
Demos are heterogeneous but useful as examples of a family: e.g. in one demo a 9 singleton became 4 while a 9 ray extended downward and another 9 stripe appeared; in another 9 singletons became 4 and horizontal 9 runs appeared; other examples used 0/8/4, 8/1/4, 7/6/4 or 3/9/4 combinations. There is no single palette mapping from the examples alone. Treat original sparse cells and boundary bands as structural cues; infer which rays/stripes are selected from the full arrangement and compare exact changed-cell deltas.

## Confirmed test result from this instance
Input was 17x20, background 6, boundary color 2: rows 1–8 have a left-edge vertical segment in column 0, and rows 9–16 have a right-edge segment in column 19. Sparse color-5 cells occur at zero-based `(1,16),(3,7),(4,6),(5,5),(7,4),(8,16)`. The accepted output preserved all 2 boundary cells and the background except for these validated additions:

- Each sparse 5 is recolored to 4.
- On rows 1, 3, 4, 5, 7, and 8, color 5 extends leftward from the respective sparse cell through columns 1..(seed_col-1); the left boundary cell at column 0 stays 2. Thus the rays end at the edge guide, with the source point encoded as 4.
- In the lower section, rows 9, 11, 12, 13, 15, and 16 are filled with 5 in columns 0..18, preserving the right boundary 2 in column 19. Rows 10 and 14 remain unchanged. These alternating full-width bands are essential; a submission containing only upper marker rays was incorrect.
- All unmentioned cells remain unchanged.

This full test behavior was accepted by the evaluator. The exact two-color ray/alternating-band rule has only this test confirmation; use fresh demos on recurrence rather than assuming every layout has the same lower-row phase.

## Additional confirmed recurrence (22x6 test)
A separate accepted test used background 9, edge-guide color 1, and one sparse color-8 marker. The guide was a right-edge vertical run at column 5, rows 5–10, and a left-edge vertical run at column 0, rows 16–21; the marker was at `(5,2)`. The accepted delta was:

- Recolor the marker `(5,2)` to 4 and extend its color 8 rightward into columns 3–4, stopping before the right-edge guide at column 5.
- In row 16 only, fill columns 1–5 with color 8, preserving the left-edge guide at column 0. Rows 17–21 remained unchanged despite continuing edge-guide cells.
- All other cells remained unchanged.

This shows the edge-run phase/extent can control which rows/columns receive extensions; do not assume every edge-guide cell is filled, or infer that a marker always extends toward a particular fixed side. Keep candidate edits narrow and use demos to determine which edge segment portions participate. This is an additional confirmed palette/orientation instance, not enough to replace demo-based inference for new layouts.

## Additional confirmed recurrence (21x27 test)
A further accepted test had background 8, guide color 9, and sparse color-3 markers. The left guide occupied column 0, rows 4–11; the right guide occupied column 26, rows 13–20. Every sparse 3 marker was recolored to 4. In the upper section, each marker on rows 4, 6, 7, 9, 10, and 11 generated a horizontal color-3 run extending toward the left guide, stopping before column 0 (which remained 9). The marker at `(7,2)` therefore yielded color 3 at column 1 and 4 at column 2; markers farther right similarly filled the gap between the left guide and the anchor. The lower section generated full-width color-3 bands, preserving the right-edge guide: rows 13, 15, 16, 18, 19, and 20 had color 3 in columns 0–25 and color 9 at column 26; rows 14 and 17 were unchanged. This confirms the orientation-reversed counterpart of earlier accepted cases: a left guide can receive rays, and selected lower rows can be filled from the left edge to just before a right guide. Preserve dimensions and every unmentioned cell. The exact lower-row phase is determined by the layout and should still be checked against demos; this test's selected rows were 13, 15, 16, 18–20.

## Failed guesses / cautions
Two earlier submissions that only painted the visible leftward rays from the six 5 markers and recolored their anchors were wrong because they omitted the lower alternating full-width 5 bands. A further attempted output was also rejected; binary feedback gives no localization. The final accepted result incorporated both upper rays and the lower selected bands. Avoid repeating the upper-only hypothesis. When demos permit, write out exact added-cell coordinates and test all unchanged cells; do not replace palette or geometry by analogy.

## Additional unresolved recurrence (5x17 test; 8 demos, 8 rejected guesses)
The test had 5 rows and 17 columns:
- r0: eight 6s, then nine 9s
- r1: all 9
- r2: `9 9 1 1 1 9 9 1` then nine 9s
- r3: `1 1 9 9 9 9 1` then ten 9s
- r4: nine 9s, then eight 6s.

All eight demo requests had been spent. Demos were highly varied and established no simple universal extrapolation. Exact qualitative changes:
1. 26x23, bg5, guides 8 at top row cols4–7 and bottom row cols0–3, sparse 3 at (3,4),(4,5). Output painted vertical 3 stripes in cols0–1 rows0–24, and 3 in (r1-2,c4-5), recolored original anchors to 4.
2. 23x17, bg2, guide7 at left edge rows0–4 and right edge rows12–16, sparse 0 markers at (12,3),(13,4),(14,7),(15,3),(16,6). Output recolored background to 0 across the left guide-aligned top rectangle rows0–4, cols1–16, and extended 0 rightward from markers on their rows through c15, marker pixels became 4, preserving guide7.
3. 12x5, bg1, left edge 8 rows5–7, right edge8 rows9–11, marker3 at (6,3),(7,3). Output extended 3 leftward on rows6–7 through c1 and markers→4; row10–11 got 3 across c0–3 while preserving right-edge 8.
4. 24x12 bg2, upper-left edge run of 0 at r0 c5–6, lower-right run r23 c10–11, isolated 3 at (6,5),(18,6). Output extended vertical 3 downward at c5 rows1–5 (with source at r6→4), vertical at c6 rows7–17; full 3 blocks top right c10–11 rows0–22; lower left expanded from c0–4 on rows18–20; both markers→4. Complex asymmetric layout.
5. 27x21 bg2, upper-right guide1 r0–2 c20, lower-left guide1 r22–24 c0; markers6 at (23,14),(24,3). Output painted 6 across rows1–2 cols0–19 (top block), and row23 c1–13 plus marker c14→4, row24 c1–2 plus marker c3→4 and row23(?) other runs; preserve guides. Direction/selection nontrivial.
6. 7x23 bg2, top-left 8 r0 c0–10, bottom 8 r6 c12–22, sparse7s around r1–4. Output made vertical 7 structures in cols0–4 and 6–9 for rows1–6, marker subset→4; right-side original 7 motifs mostly preserved with select markers recolored 4; bottom guide preserved.
7. 6x24 bg9, top-right guide7 r0 c15–23 and bottom-left guide7 r5 c2–10, marker2 at (1,10). Output extends 2 down column10 rows2–4 and to right edge column23 rows1–5; source→4; guides preserved.
8. 30x18 bg3, top-right guide6 rows0–6 c17, lower-left guide6 rows17–23 c0, markers8 at (18,5),(19,12),(20,12),(21,2). Output repainted top rectangle rows1–4 cols0–16 as8; lower rays/blocks from markers toward both edge regions, with select source cells→4; guides preserved.

Our eight rejected submissions on the test were:
1. Rays/edge-fill guess: rows1 all c0–7=1; r2 c0–1=1, anchors c2–4 and c7→4; r3 c0–1=4 and c2–5=1, c6=4; other cells preserved.
2. Same but full color-1 row1 except c8 and similar r2/r3 (overextended edge fill).
3. Same broad filling with some selector variations (r2/r3 broad 1 fill).
4. Repeated a near-original sparse-marker recoloring/ray form.
5. Tried preserving background/markers with partial outputs, wrong.
6. Inferred cross-boundary global fills, wrong.
7. Alternative set of broad rays/blocks, wrong.
8. Final attempt changed r1 to color1 c0–4,c6–7, r2 c0–2=1, c3–4=4,c6=1,c7=4, r3 c0–1=4; wrong.

Critical caution: none of these failed guesses localizes why they are wrong. Do not repeat any of these outputs or simply adjust color/extent. Despite task-id recurrence and eight elaborate demos, the rule remains unresolved; examples have varying palettes, layouts, guide orientation, and apparently selected marker rays/rectangles. No well-supported exact target answer was found. On future recurrence, acquire live demos and explicitly infer selector using exact changed AND unchanged spans. A task ID match or the prior skill's accepted test case does not establish the current geometry's detailed rule. Preserve input if not selected; never submit a guessed fill rule on the basis of analogy alone.

## Fresh unresolved recurrence (6x24 test; 8 demos and 8 rejected outputs)
A further live instance again showed only family-level behavior, not a uniquely determined selector. Test input: background 2; color-1 guide bands at row 0, columns 0–6 and row 5, columns 13–19; sparse color-0 markers at `(2,18)` and `(3,14)` (zero-based). All eight available demonstrations had varied guide layouts, marker layouts, palette/orientation, and outputs. Do not transfer any accepted old geometry mechanically.

Exact live-demo deltas and preservation evidence:
1. 5x11, background 0, guide 6 at left edge rows 1–2 and right edge rows 3–4; markers 8 at `(1,5),(2,6)`. Both markers became 4; rows 1–2 filled with 8 from c1 to just before the marker, preserving guide c0; rows 3–4 filled 8 across c0–9, preserving guide c10.
2. 6x27, background 0, guide 8 at right edge rows 0–1 and left edge rows 2–3; marker 7 at `(2,16)`. Marker→4; row 0 filled 7 at c0–25 (right guide preserved), and row 2 filled c1–15 toward the left guide. Other rows unchanged.
3. 11x24, background 1, guide 8 top-left r0 c0–4 and bottom-left r10 c6–10; markers 0 at `(3,8),(3,10),(5,6)`. Output adds vertical 0 stripes in c0,c2,c4 over rows 1–10; the three listed marker pixels become 4; retain remaining cells, including unselected sparse pattern positions, as shown.
4. 17x12, background 3, guide 8 at r0 c7–10 and r16 c0–3; markers 9 at `(2,7),(11,9),(13,10)`. Each source marker became 4. Output adds selected vertical 9 bands/columns around c0,c2,c3 and c9,c10 with differing extents; many other background cells remain untouched. This is not a uniform fill of all marker columns.
5. 13x16, background 9, guide 0 on left edge rows 5–8 and right edge rows 9–12; markers 5 at `(5,3),(7,13),(8,11)`. All three markers→4; rows 5,7,8 extend 5 leftward from c1 to just before each marker, preserving left guide c0. In lower section, rows 9,11,12 fill c0–14 with 5, preserving right guide c15; row 10 unchanged.
6. 9x18, background 8, guide 2 at left edge rows 0–2 and right edge rows 6–8; markers 7 at `(6,3),(7,7)`. Both markers→4; rows 0–1 fill 7 in c1–17, preserving right guide; rows 6–7 fill from just right of marker through c16. Other rows unchanged.
7. 17x25, background 8, guide 3 across top-right r0 c15–24 and bottom-left r16 c3–12; sparse 2s at `(3,9),(4,7),(5,6),(7,5),(7,11),(8,12),(10,3),(11,4),(11,8),(11,10)`. All listed markers became 4; output paints a broad right-side 2 field and selected left-side connected/column regions, with many intermediate cells and untouched gaps. Exact output included upper right c15–24 for rows1–15 and progressive lower/left structures, not simply one ray per marker.
8. 28x11, background 9, guide 3 at top row c5–7 and bottom row c0–2; markers 0 at `(2,6),(14,7)`. Both markers→4; output fills columns1–2 with 0 for rows0–26 and extends color 0 vertically in c7 around the lower marker (rows1–13), preserving both guide rows and leaving other cells unchanged.

First test attempt (a sparse 0/4 recolor plus guessed alternating vertical 0/2 columns) was rejected. The remaining seven submissions were also rejected, including near-preservation/marker-only variants, altered stripe placement, broad stripe blocks on both sides of the markers, a malformed row-width payload, and broad zero-filled rectangles. Binary rejection gives no localization. Consequently there is no supported exact test selector or output from this recurrence. Do not submit these guesses again or make cosmetic variations; on a future recurrence, derive a new selector from exact live deltas and negative evidence. The demos show that color-4 marker encoding, edge-guided extensions, remote bands, and selective unpainted spans can all occur, but not which operations apply to this test's two markers and guides.

## Fresh accepted recurrence (25x16 test; 4 demos, one wrong submission)
This new test used background 5, edge-guide color 2, and sparse color-6 marks. Guides were on the top edge at row 0, columns 3–8, and bottom edge at row 24, columns 10–15. Sparse 6s were at zero-based `(6,7)`, `(15,8)`, `(21,5)`, `(21,6)`. The accepted output made exactly these changes:

- Fill color 6 in rows 0–23, columns 12–15 inclusive (a 24x4 rectangle); leave the bottom guide at row 24 unchanged.
- Fill color 6 in rows 1–14, columns 5–6 inclusive, and rows 1–14 at column 8.
- Recolor each of the four original sparse 6 markers to 4, including the adjacent pair `(21,5),(21,6)`.
- Preserve every other input cell, including the top and bottom guide segments and all background gaps.

The first submission made the same edits except it missed the four cells in row 0, columns 12–15; it was rejected. Adding precisely that top-row segment yielded acceptance. This is a test-specific confirmation; don't turn this geometry into a universal selector.

The four demos on that instance remain heterogeneous and illustrate why selector and preserved cells matter. Demo 1 (24x17) had background 2, guide 8 top row cols 7–16 and bottom row cols 7–13, plus 0 markers `(10,12),(15,10),(20,13)`. Output added repeated vertical 0 stripes at cols 3,5,6 for rows 1–22, and in the lower area added stripes at cols 10 and 12, with original markers encoded as 4 and guide cells preserved. Demo 2 (6x29), background 3, top guide 1 at row 0 cols16–24 and bottom guide 1 at row5 cols0–8; sparse 7 marks at `(2,20),(2,21),(2,24),(3,19)`. Output filled 7 at cols3–5 in rows0–4 and at col8 in rows0–4; the selected marks at `(2,21),(2,24),(3,19)` became 4, while `(2,20)` stayed 7. Demo 3 (24x29), background 0, left guide 7 rows7–11 col0 and right guide 7 rows19–23 col28; sparse 6 marks `(7,14),(9,21),(10,22),(11,10)`. Output extended 6 across selected spans toward guides, with source marks becoming 4 at `(7,14),(9,21),(11,10)` but the mark `(10,22)` remained 6; remote horizontal bands also appeared. Demo 4 (22x29), background 5, top guide 6 row0 cols5–13 and bottom guide 6 row21 cols20–28; sparse 0 marks `(8,8),(14,13),(17,10)`. Output included long vertical 0 columns/stripes at cols8,10,13 and 23,25,28, with source marks selectively encoded as 4 at `(8,8),(14,13),(17,10)`; unchanged regions constrain the selector.

This recurrence confirms selective marker-to-4 encoding and guide-related extended structures can coexist, but no single general rule was proven by these varied examples. The accepted test's precise delta above is the reliable result; do not transfer other recurrences' stripe orientation or marker selection blindly.

## Procedure
1. Inventory border-colored line segments, sparse pixels, and background; identify all distinct colors and orientations.
2. Diff every demo exactly. Separate source marker recolors (often to 4 in these examples) from long painted rays or bands.
3. Infer the selector/phase from the boundary geometry and marker arrangement, including alternating or remote stripes; do not only extrapolate nearest-neighbor lines.
4. Validate the complete predicted delta against all demos, retaining every unchanged area.
5. Validate rectangular dimensions and output literal before submitting.

# Cost-sensitive ARC demo selection

Use this class-level workflow in ARC benchmarks where requesting another input-output example and submitting a wrong answer both incur cost.

## Procedure

1. **Inventory uncertainty.** Write down the leading materially different candidate rules, including their predicted output differences on the current test. Separate uncertainty about palette mapping, geometry, selected objects/rows, orientation, and phase.
2. **Pick a discriminating observation.** Before requesting a demo, state what exact observed feature would distinguish the leading hypotheses. A useful demo should provide evidence that can update the rule, not merely resemble the test or reinforce broad visual vocabulary.
3. **Compare value and cost.** A demo request and a wrong submission may cost the same. Request only when the example is likely to separate plausible hypotheses enough to improve expected accuracy; otherwise submit the best-supported hypothesis rather than requesting reflexively.
4. **Analyze the complete pair.** Record dimensions, colors, and exact changed-cell coordinates. Account for both changed and unchanged regions. Derive the operation from the full delta, not from a visually salient subset.
5. **Factor shared mechanics from variable selectors.** Across heterogeneous examples, distinguish stable components (for example, marker recoloring or a ray stopping before a guide) from variable choices (which marker, segment, direction, rows, or phase are selected). Shared colors or boundary geometry do not prove a single global selector.
6. **Update beliefs after every example.** Eliminate candidates contradicted by the example; retain unresolved alternatives explicitly. If a result does not discriminate, do not simply request another similar example—refine the competing hypotheses and the desired distinguishing feature first.
7. **Stop gathering evidence when enough is known.** Validate a complete output against all examples, including preservation of cells not predicted to change, then submit. Preserve attempts for genuinely different hypotheses and never repeat an unchanged rejected output without concrete new evidence.

## Common pitfalls

- Asking for several examples without a specific question wastes budget; broad examples can reveal family mechanics while leaving the test's selector unresolved.
- Treating one task ID, palette, or edge-guide motif as proof of a fixed detailed rule is unsafe when recurrence layouts differ.
- Explaining only the apparent changed feature is insufficient: selectors may be encoded by remote bands, edge segments, phase, or exceptions.
- Do not respond to uncertainty by emitting speculative output grids without first checking whether a single targeted demo is worth the same cost.

## Validation checklist

- [ ] Competing hypotheses are explicit and materially distinct.
- [ ] A requested demo has a named discriminating purpose.
- [ ] Complete input/output deltas and unchanged areas were checked.
- [ ] Shared mechanics are separated from layout-dependent selection.
- [ ] Final action follows the benchmark schema exactly.

1. Record dimensions, palette, apparent background, source objects, and candidate markers.

1. Reconstruct the demonstration delta exactly: list all changed and unchanged cells/objects and their coordinates. Treat unchanged objects as constraints, not background noise.
